initialization_boundary.reason: The initialization session inspected current public sources only to verify benchmark scope. Those observations must not anchor the sealed blind atlas.

cycle_hypothesis.statement: DRAM and NAND share major suppliers, capital-allocation constraints and broad memory-cycle forces, but may lead, lag or diverge at specific turning points.
cycle_hypothesis.test_rule: Use one historical time grid and shared-company view, while preserving product-line-specific price, inventory, technology, demand and supply metrics.

passes.focus: shared memory upswing, tight supply, pricing power and supplier investment response
questions: Recall DRAM and NAND price, inventory, bit supply/demand, technology transitions, capex, supplier actions and contemporaneous narratives on the same time grid.
Where did the two product lines move together, and where did one lead or lag the other?

passes.focus: downcycle, pandemic demand shifts, inventory and renewed tightness
questions: Separate PC, server, mobile and storage demand narratives from comparable observations for each product line.
Recall supplier cuts, capex decisions, node/layer transitions and forecasts that were later revised.

passes.focus: inventory correction, price decline, production cuts and capex discipline
questions: Recall when different actors recognized DRAM and NAND inventory problems and how expected normalization timing changed.
Look for product-line lead/lag, write-downs, utilization changes, failed demand narratives and cross-product capital-allocation responses.

passes.focus: HBM/AI mix shift, conventional DRAM interaction, enterprise SSD/NAND demand, capacity allocation and technology constraints
questions: Recall HBM qualification/ramp expectations separately from later outcomes.
Recall NAND/SSD demand, layer/QLC transitions, bit supply, capex and inventory alongside DRAM/HBM conditions without merging the metrics.
Recall DRAM product-generation transitions, applications, qualification timing, supply constraints and pricing/mix implications.
Do not assume product generations or supplier node labels are directly comparable.
Recall NAND layer/generation, bits-per-cell, product and qualification transitions by period.
Keep raw NAND, packaged flash and finished SSD metrics distinct; do not assume layer labels across suppliers are equivalent.
Exhaust Samsung, SK hynix and Micron by period across both DRAM and NAND, splitting product-line facts where the source allows.
Recall company-level capex, inventory, utilization, cuts and product-mix choices that require cross-product interpretation.
Recall DRAM-specific actors including CXMT, Nanya and specialty suppliers, and NAND-specific actors including Kioxia, Western Digital/SanDisk and YMTC.
Preserve actor membership by product line rather than forcing a single shared supplier list.
Recall definitions and periods where each metric became non-comparable or especially important.
Identify likely primary or methodology-bearing source families for later verification without searching now.
Recall mechanisms linking price, inventory, utilization, capex, technology migration, bit growth, qualification and effective supply for DRAM and NAND separately.
Recall cross-product mechanisms through shared company capital budgets, cleanroom/equipment constraints, customer cycles and supply-discipline decisions.
Treat DRAM/NAND co-cycling as a hypothesis to test, not a preloaded conclusion.
Recall consensus, minority views, shortage/oversupply narratives, inventory normalization forecasts and capex-discipline claims by product line and period.
Recall contemporaneous views on whether DRAM and NAND were synchronized, decoupling, or expected to recover at different times.
Recall DRAM node labels, NAND layer/generation labels, old product names, fab/JV/company names, pricing terms, report-title phrases and terminology useful for lost-web search.
Prefer vocabulary that a current searcher would not naturally guess.
Recall delayed fabs, failed/slow ramps, qualification misses, utilization cuts, write-downs, cancelled investments and product narratives that did not materialize across DRAM and NAND.
Include technologies or actors that mattered historically but later became marginal.
Work backward to earlier demand, inventory, capex, technology, supply and customer-ordering conditions for both DRAM and NAND.
Use the later downturn only to activate leads; never present the later outcome as information already known earlier.

passes.anchor: 2024-2026 AI-driven HBM and storage mix changes
questions: Recall earlier HBM, packaging, NAND/SSD, customer, accelerator and supplier decisions that may have set up later product-mix changes.
Separate what was genuinely anticipated from what only became obvious later.

Recall semiconductor equipment, packaging, foundry/base-die, cloud capex, GPU/platform, handset/PC, storage systems, geopolitics, export controls and financing variables that directly changed DRAM or NAND conditions.
Do not expand adjacent sectors beyond claim-scoped memory effects.
For each famous memory-cycle explanation generate at least two contemporaneously plausible alternatives.
State what historical evidence would distinguish common-cycle explanations from product-line-specific explanations.
Inspect the time × actor × product-line × metric matrix for suspicious blanks.
Ask what long-tenured DRAM and NAND operators would each say is missing if the atlas looks too much like a public market report.
Cluster duplicate leads and classify remaining gaps.
Judge whether three consecutive orthogonal passes have produced few new high-importance non-duplicate leads across both product lines.

recursive_questions_for_high_importance_: Who else? Which other actors or product lines are connected?
What preceded it? Which earlier indicators or decisions existed?
What followed it? Which later actions or observations may be connected?
What was it called then? Which historical vocabulary should later search use?

objectives: resolve vague memory leads into exact company, fab, product, report and historical terminology
locate claim-scoped primary sources before secondary summaries
separate independent sources from repeated syndication
forbidden: promote search snippets into Fact or Judgment
delete a lead because search returns not found
treat repeated secondary coverage as independent proof
merge DRAM and NAND metrics merely because they co-move
